extracted.intended_audience: public company management, corporate counsel, investor relations professionals, and finance teams preparing earnings releases, SEC filings, and other public disclosures
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for preparing, labeling, presenting and reconciling non-GAAP financial measures in SEC filings, earnings releases, analyst decks, webcasts and other public communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present GAAP measures with equal or greater prominence
rubrics_metrics.description: Where non-GAAP measures are presented in an earnings release or another SEC filing that is subject to Regulation G, SEC rules require that the corresponding GAAP measure be presented with equal or greater prominence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best practices: present the GAAP metric and reconciliation prominently; do not rely on presenting GAAP later in the filing. If non-GAAP is emphasized (bullet points, quotes), ensure the corresponding GAAP measure is given equal or greater prominence. Avoid describing non-GAAP metrics with superlatives (e.g., “exceptional”, “record performance”) unless analogous descriptors are used for the GAAP measure. Formatting matters: GAAP and non-GAAP must use the same formatting (no bolding or larger fonts for non-GAAP when GAAP is not similarly formatted).

rubrics_metrics.name: GAAP measures should always precede non-GAAP measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Where non-GAAP measures are presented in an earnings release or another SEC filing subject to Regulation G, the non-GAAP measure should always be preceded by the corresponding GAAP measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing the GAAP metric and the relevant reconciliation later in the filing is not sufficient; present GAAP first on the face of the disclosure where Regulation G applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay special attention to bullet points and quotes
rubrics_metrics.description: When an earnings release emphasizes non-GAAP financial measures—by including them in bullet points at the beginning of the release or in a management quote—the release must present the corresponding GAAP measure with equal or greater prominence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid front-loading non-GAAP numbers in headline bullets/quotes without the comparable GAAP measure presented equally prominently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be careful with superlatives
rubrics_metrics.description: The SEC Staff considers describing a non-GAAP metric with superlatives without providing analogous descriptors when presenting the corresponding GAAP measure to be a violation of the 'equal or greater prominence' requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use adjectives like 'exceptional' or 'record' only for non-GAAP metrics; apply similar language context to the comparable GAAP measure or avoid the superlative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand difference between financial metrics and operational metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Operating and other statistical measures (e.g., unit sales, numbers of employees or customers) or ratios/statistical measures calculated using only GAAP financial measures and/or operating measures are excluded from the SEC’s definition of a non-GAAP financial measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if excluded, best practice is to provide definitions and explanatory information for such metrics or other KPIs so investors can understand calculations and comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconciliation must be to the most directly comparable GAAP measure
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulation G requires that the contemplated reconciliation be made to the most directly comparable GAAP measure, even where that GAAP measure is not presented on the face of the financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if presenting 'adjusted gross profit', reconcile to GAAP gross profit; ensure the chosen GAAP comparator is the most directly comparable line item.

rubrics_metrics.name: No de minimis exception to reconciliations
rubrics_metrics.description: A reconciliation is required with respect to a non-GAAP financial measure regardless of the size of the difference between the non-GAAP financial measure and the corresponding GAAP financial measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even small adjustments require a reconciliation; do not omit reconciliation on the basis the difference is immaterial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of non-GAAP financial measures
rubrics_metrics.description: A non-GAAP financial measure is a numerical measure of a registrant's historical or future financial performance, financial position or cash flows that includes or excludes amounts (or is subject to adjustments that include or exclude amounts) that are included in or excluded from the most directly comparable GAAP measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-GAAP measures exclude operating/statistical measures and measures required by GAAP/Commission rules; if two registrants use the same name, they may calculate it differently—always disclose calculation methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common non-GAAP financial measures (examples and cautions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commonly used non-GAAP measures include EBIT, EBITDA, adjusted earnings (adjusted net income), adjusted earnings per share, free cash flow, funds from operations (FFO) and many others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per-share liquidity measures (e.g., cash flow per share) are specifically prohibited by Regulation G. Before adding other non-GAAP measures ensure they are permissible and properly defined and reconciled; describe how each measure is calculated because names can be used inconsistently across registrants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of non-GAAP financial measures in SEC filings (Item 10(e) of Regulation S-K)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever a non-GAAP financial measure is included in an SEC filing (e.g., 10-K, 10-Q, Form 8-K earnings release), the registrant must include required disclosures and reconciliations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required components: (A) presentation, with equal or greater prominence, of the most directly comparable GAAP measure; (B) a reconciliation (quantitative for historical measures; quantitative to the extent available for forward-looking measures); (C) a statement disclosing why management believes the non-GAAP measure provides useful information to investors (not required in 10-Q if in most recent 10-K); and (D) to the extent material, a statement disclosing additional purposes management uses the measure for.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of non-GAAP financial measures in other public disclosures (Regulation G)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a non-GAAP financial measure is included in a public disclosure not filed with the SEC, the registrant must include a presentation of the most directly comparable GAAP measure and a reconciliation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reconciliation must be quantitative for historical measures and quantitative to the extent available for forward-looking information. There is no requirement to present the reconciliation with equal or greater prominence in disclosures not filed with the SEC, but best practices on prominence still apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-GAAP adjustments that change GAAP recognition/measurement are individually tailored and may be misleading
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-GAAP adjustments that have the effect of changing the recognition and measurement principles required to be applied in accordance with GAAP would be considered individually tailored and may be misleading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include accelerating revenue recognition that GAAP recognizes ratably, presenting revenue net when GAAP requires gross (or vice versa), or switching from accrual to cash basis for a non-GAAP performance measure. Such adjustments could draw SEC comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application to foreign private issuers (FPIs)
rubrics_metrics.description: For FPIs whose primary financial statements are prepared under non-U.S. GAAP, 'GAAP' for non-GAAP rules refers to the principles under which those primary statements are prepared; if a non-GAAP measure is derived from a U.S. GAAP measure, GAAP refers to U.S. GAAP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain prohibitions under Item 10(e) may be permitted for FPIs if: (1) the measure relates to the accounting principles used in the FPI's primary financial statements; (2) the measure is required or expressly permitted by the standard-setter responsible for those principles; and (3) the measure is included in the FPI's annual report used in its home jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited non-GAAP adjustments and presentations
rubrics_metrics.description: When a non-GAAP measure is included in an SEC filing, the registrant must not do certain things that are expressly prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibitions include: excluding charges or liabilities that required (or will require) cash settlement from non-GAAP liquidity measures (except EBIT and EBITDA); adjusting performance measures to eliminate or smooth items labeled non-recurring/infrequent/unusual where the item is reasonably likely to recur within two years or a similar item occurred within prior two years; presenting non-GAAP measures on the face of GAAP financial statements or notes; presenting non-GAAP measures on face of pro forma financial information required by Article 11 of Regulation S-X; and using titles/descriptions that are the same as, or confusingly similar to, GAAP titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-applicability to business combination communications (proxy communications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 10(e) of Regulation S-K does not apply to a non-GAAP measure included in disclosure relating to a proposed business combination if the disclosure is contained in communications subject to the proxy/business combination rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications contained in materials governed by the proxy rules or business combination rules (e.g., filings under §230.425, §240.14a-12, §240.14d-2(b)(2), §229.1015) are excepted from Item 10(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-written disclosures (webcasts, broadcasts, oral remarks) — website posting and disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: If a non-GAAP measure is made public orally, telephonically, by webcast, broadcast or similar means, Regulation G’s requirements may be satisfied by timely website posting and disclosure of the location during the presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the required GAAP comparator and reconciliation on the registrant's website at the time the non-GAAP measure is made public and publicly disclose the location and availability during the presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proxy statement CD&A target levels exception (Instruction 5 to Item 402(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure in the CD&A of a proxy statement of target levels that are non-GAAP financial measures are not subject to Regulation G and Item 10(e), but disclosure must be provided as to how the number is calculated from the registrant's audited financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relief is limited to CD&A target levels; other pay-related non-GAAP disclosures remain subject to Regulation G/Item 10(e) although staff may permit cross-references or annex placement for required reconciliations in certain circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forward-looking non-GAAP measures and projections — reconciliation expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 10(e) and Regulation G require a reconciliation for forward-looking non-GAAP information, but the reconciliation need not be quantitative unless the reconciling information is available without unreasonable efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reconciling information is not available without unreasonable efforts, the issuer must disclose that the comparable GAAP measure is not accessible, identify the unavailable reconciling information, and disclose the probable significance of the unavailable information. Effective July 2024, Item 10(b) amendments require projections with non-GAAP measures to include a clear definition/explanation, description of the most directly comparable GAAP measure, and explanation why the non-GAAP measure was selected instead of a GAAP measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-applicability to certain registrants (investment companies and limited FPI circumstances)
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirements of Item 10(e) do not apply to registered investment companies; under certain conditions the requirements do not apply to FPIs making disclosures outside the U.S. or using non-U.S. GAAP measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FPI relief conditions include (i) securities listed outside the U.S., (ii) non-GAAP measure not derived from U.S. GAAP, and (iii) disclosure made outside the U.S. or in communications released outside the U.S.; even where not technically required, non-compliance can raise anti-fraud issues if a company voluntarily continues public reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit committee oversight of non-GAAP use
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant’s audit committee should consider the registrant’s use of non-GAAP financial measures in its financial reporting as part of its oversight responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audit committees (and boards) should review the type and presentation of information in earnings press releases, paying particular attention to 'pro forma' or 'adjusted' non-GAAP information; best practice regardless of listing (NYSE, Nasdaq) is active committee review of earnings releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustments excluding normal, recurring cash operating expenses can be misleading
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain adjustments—although not explicitly prohibited—may violate Rule 100(b) of Regulation G because they cause the presentation of the non-GAAP measure to be misleading (for example, excluding normal recurring cash operating expenses necessary to operate the business).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether an adjustment is misleading depends on the company’s facts and circumstances. The staff evaluates the nature and effect of adjustments and how they relate to operations, revenue generation, business strategy, industry and regulatory environment; recurring is judged by nature and effect and frequency (including irregular intervals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inconsistent presentation between periods may be misleading; recast prior periods when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: A non-GAAP measure presented inconsistently between periods (e.g., adjusting a current period charge but not similar prior-period charges) can violate Rule 100(b) unless the change is disclosed and explained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depending on significance, it may be necessary to recast prior-period non-GAAP measures to conform to the current presentation and place the disclosure in appropriate context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluding charges but not excluding gains can be misleading
rubrics_metrics.description: A non-GAAP measure that adjusts for non-recurring charges but does not adjust for non-recurring gains occurring in the same period could violate Rule 100(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjustments should be symmetric and consistent; excluding only costs (or only gains) where both occurred is misleading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate labeling or failure to clearly describe non-GAAP measures is misleading
rubrics_metrics.description: A non-GAAP measure must be appropriately labeled and clearly described. Failure to identify and describe a measure as non-GAAP or using misleading labels can violate Rule 100(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of violations: labeling contribution-margin-style calculation as 'net revenue'; labeling a non-GAAP metric with the same name as a GAAP line item even though calculated differently (e.g., 'Gross Profit'); labeling a measure 'pro forma' that does not conform with Article 11 pro forma requirements. Always identify a measure as non-GAAP and disclose the nature and effect of each adjustment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensive disclosure may not cure materially misleading non-GAAP measures
rubrics_metrics.description: The staff views that a non-GAAP measure could be so misleading that even extensive, detailed disclosure about the nature and effect of each adjustment would not prevent the measure from being materially misleading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume voluminous footnote disclosure cures a fundamentally misleading presentation; redesign the measure or refrain from presenting it if it is materially misleading in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forecasts provided to financial advisors for business combinations may be excluded from non-GAAP rules if conditions met
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial measures included in forecasts provided to a financial advisor for rendering an opinion materially related to a business combination and disclosed to comply with Item 1015 of Regulation M-A or similar law may be excluded from the definition of non-GAAP financial measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The exclusion applies only to forecasts provided to financial advisors for those purposes and only to the extent they are disclosed consistent with the specified rules; consult the specific Q&A details when relying on this exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-GAAP definition exclusions and non-examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures that are not non-GAAP financial measures include operating/statistical measures (unit sales, number of subscribers), segment profit/loss measures consistent with ASC 280, disclosure of expected indebtedness or planned repayments, and estimated revenues/expenses calculated in the same manner as GAAP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also excluded are financial measures required by a system of regulation (e.g., bank capital measures). Ratios calculated using only GAAP measures or only operating measures are generally outside the non-GAAP definition (e.g., revenues per square foot where revenue is GAAP-based).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation G anti-misleading prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulation G prohibits any registrant (or person acting on its behalf) from making public a non‑GAAP financial measure that, taken together with the information accompanying it, contains an untrue statement of a material fact or omits a material fact necessary to make the presentation not misleading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an overarching anti-fraud-style prohibition that applies to presentation, labeling, reconciliation, and context; ensure disclosures are complete and not misleading in light of how the non-GAAP measure is presented.
